biomarker: RAS mutant or wild-type (KRAS G12D qualifies)

inclusion_match_notes: RASolute 303 enrolls treatment-naive metastatic PDAC and accepts the patient's KRAS G12D under its RAS-mutant criterion, matching tumor type, first line, and ECOG 1. Tissue NGS confirmation of the ctDNA G12D call strengthens the eligibility token. This is the lead enrollable option on the KRAS axis at the patient's line.

indication: previously treated metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
biomarker: RAS G12/G13/Q61 mutant or no RAS mutation; 91.8% RAS G12
design: randomized open-label, daraxonrasib vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy (RASolute 302)
inclusion_match_notes: The registration read-out for daraxonrasib: OS hazard ratio 0.40 in the RAS G12 group, which includes KRAS G12D. The trial sits at second line and the patient is treatment-naive, so it reads as the evidence base behind the first-line RASolute 303 option rather than a slot he enters now. It is the strongest efficacy anchor on the KRAS axis for this case.

design: platform study of RAS(ON) inhibitors (RMC-6236, RMC-9805) +/- chemo, cetuximab, bevacizumab
inclusion_match_notes: RMC-GI-102 has KRAS G12D subprotocols that enroll PDAC, so the patient's tumor type and allele both qualify. It gives access to the G12D-selective zoldonrasib and to combination cohorts that the single-agent phase 3 trials do not. Tissue NGS confirmation of G12D supports the eligibility token here as well.

indication: metastatic KRAS G12D-mutated pancreatic adenocarcinoma, first-line
design: randomized double-blind, zoldonrasib + investigator's-choice chemo vs placebo + chemo (RASolute 305)
inclusion_match_notes: RASolute 305 requires KRAS G12D specifically and enrolls treatment-naive metastatic PDAC, so it matches the patient on allele, tumor type, and first line. Zoldonrasib is the G12D-selective RAS(ON) agent, distinct from the pan-RAS daraxonrasib, which corrects the earlier note conflating RMC-9805 with RMC-6236. A documented tissue G12D call is the enrollment token.

indication: advanced KRAS G12D-mutant solid tumors (NSCLC, CRC, PDAC)
design: open-label dose-escalation/expansion, RMC-9805 mono or with RMC-6236
inclusion_match_notes: This first-in-human zoldonrasib basket accepts G12D PDAC but enrolls patients who have progressed on or are intolerant to standard therapy, so a treatment-naive patient does not match the line criterion yet. It becomes relevant after a first-line regimen or if he is intolerant of chemotherapy. Tumor type and allele otherwise fit.

indication: metastatic KRAS G12D-mutated PDAC, previously untreated
inclusion_match_notes: DAWN-303 requires KRAS G12D and enrolls previously untreated metastatic PDAC, matching the patient on allele, tumor type, and first line. The phase 1 read-out for INCB161734 at ASCO GI 2026 showed 37% ORR and 78% disease control in pretreated G12D PDAC, which motivates the front-line combination test. A second sponsor's G12D-selective agent broadens the front-line options beyond Revolution Medicines.

indication: advanced/metastatic KRAS G12D solid tumors incl. PDAC
design: open-label, INCB161734 mono and combinations (cetuximab, retifanlimab, gem/nab-paclitaxel, INCA33890)
inclusion_match_notes: The phase 1 parent study enrolls G12D PDAC at first line and beyond, so the patient qualifies on allele and tumor type at his current line. Combination cohorts pair the inhibitor with gem/nab-paclitaxel and with the anti-PD-1 retifanlimab. The early efficacy signal (37% ORR, 78% DCR) is the strongest single-agent G12D-PDAC response data surfaced in this search.

indication: advanced KRAS G12D solid tumors (NSCLC, CRC, PDAC)
inclusion_match_notes: Included for mechanism context: MRTX1133 was the first clinical KRAS G12D-selective small molecule and its program was terminated for formulation problems, not lack of target validity. The board should see that the first-generation G12D drug stalled on drug-like properties while later agents (zoldonrasib, INCB161734) carried the mechanism forward. Not an enrollable option.

indication: KRAS/NRAS-mutated PDAC and colorectal cancer, adjuvant/MRD
biomarker: KRAS/NRAS G12D, G12R, G12V, G12A, G12C, G12S, G13D
design: single-arm amphiphile vaccine (AMPLIFY-7P; phase 1 AMPLIFY-201 reported)
inclusion_match_notes: ELI-002 covers G12D and is not restricted to a single HLA allele, so the patient's class I genotype does not exclude it. The trial enrolls the adjuvant minimal-residual-disease setting after resection, which does not match newly diagnosed unresectable metastatic disease, so the row is informational for the KRAS-vaccine axis rather than enrollable. The phase 1 AMPLIFY-201 data (84% T-cell responses, median RFS 16.3 months) anchor the vaccine mechanism.

biomarker: mutant KRAS incl. G12D (n=4 of cohort)

inclusion_match_notes: A pooled mutant-KRAS peptide vaccine, not single-allele-restricted, so the patient's HLA type does not foreclose it; four of twelve treated patients carried G12D. The trial enrolls resected PDAC in the adjuvant setting, which does not fit unresectable metastatic disease, so the row documents the vaccine-plus-checkpoint mechanism rather than offering enrollment. It also shows the checkpoint pairing being tested in an immunologically cold, mostly MSS PDAC population.
sponsor: Johns Hopkins (Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center)

indication: advanced/metastatic KRAS G12D solid tumors (NSCLC, CRC, PDAC, endometrial)
biomarker: KRAS G12D + HLA-C*08:02 (NT-112 arm) or HLA-A*11:01/11:02 (AZD0240 arm)

The KRAS G12D target and PDAC tumor type fit, but the HLA gate excludes him from both products, so the row exists to document that the published C*08:02-restricted anti-G12D TCR-T does not apply here. This is the concrete HLA-screening result the case flagged.
intervention_dosing: single autologous T-cell infusion after lymphodepletion

inclusion_match_notes: The Merck/Moderna mRNA KRAS vaccine required HLA-A*11:01 and/or HLA-C*08:02, neither of which the patient carries, so the HLA gate excludes him even though the construct included G12D. The program was terminated for business reasons. Kept as informational context: an HLA-restricted mRNA KRAS vaccine that this patient's genotype would have screened out regardless.

design: ceralasertib alone and with olaparib or durvalumab, ARID1A-stratified
intervention: ceralasertib (AZD6738), ATR inhibitor +/- olaparib or durvalumab
inclusion_match_notes: This ATR-inhibitor study accepts pancreatic cancer and assigns treatment by ARID1A/BAF250a status, so it directly targets the patient's secondary synthetic-lethal axis via a basket that takes his tumor type. The match is partial because eligibility turns on BAF250a loss by IHC, and only about two-thirds of ARID1A-mutant tumors show protein loss, so the frameshift call alone does not confirm entry. ARID1A IHC is the validation step before this becomes concrete.
sponsor: University of California San Francisco / AstraZeneca

design: tuvusertib + DDR inhibitor or checkpoint inhibitor (DDRiver Solid Tumors 320)
inclusion_match_notes: Tuvusertib is an ATR inhibitor with an ARID1A loss-of-function cohort, so it targets the patient's synthetic-lethal axis, but the named ARID1A arm centers on endometrial cancer rather than PDAC. Whether a pancreatic patient enters depends on the broader solid-tumor eligibility and on confirmed ARID1A protein loss. Included as mechanism support for the ATR axis; check the current protocol for tumor-type breadth.

indication: solid tumors with ARID1A mutation (incl. pancreas)
design: single-arm tazemetostat in ARID1A-mutant solid tumors
inclusion_match_notes: This basket targeted the EZH2 arm of the ARID1A synthetic-lethal hypothesis and explicitly listed pancreas among eligible tumor types, so it matched the patient's secondary axis on both biomarker and tumor type. Ipsen discontinued tazemetostat trials in March 2026 on an unfavorable benefit-risk read, so the row is now informational. The board should weigh that the EZH2 route in ARID1A-deficient solid tumors lost its lead agent while the ATR route remains active.

design: camonsertib + niraparib or olaparib (ATTACC), molecularly selected
inclusion_match_notes: ATTACC tested the ATR inhibitor camonsertib with a PARP inhibitor in molecularly selected solid tumors, a design relevant to the ARID1A axis, but the trial was terminated when the sponsor did not run the phase 2 expansion. ARID1A's place in the selected-biomarker list and pancreatic eligibility are not confirmed from the registry text. Kept as ATR-axis mechanism context rather than an open option.
